question.hook: why are eye patches so popular these days?

insights.headline: In eye-mask carousels the win comes from tiny, cinematic 1-4 word hooks and comparison/scene framing (comparison, relatable_scenario and story_tease all lift 3.43, medians 400,987-630,623 views) — save the before/after and the collagen science for the swipe, not the first panel.

winningPatterns.pattern: Ultra-short, 1-4 word hooks that read like a film title, not a caption
winningPatterns.evidence: Seven of the top-ranked hooks are 1-4 words: "My mask" (630,623 | 198.3x), "mask on" (617,895), "Mask on Mask off" (540,836 | 35.5x), "Real eyes.." (513,347 | 105.8x), "High Collagen" (261,137 | 4080.3x), "eyes" (251,376 | 72.7x), "hey, mask!" (219,916 | 28.9x).
winningPatterns.howToApply: Cap slide 1 at four words set large over a close-up of patched under-eyes. Let the image carry the information; put the product name, the claim and the routine on slides 2-6.

winningPatterns.pattern: Comparison / scene / tease framing beats claim framing by a wide margin
winningPatterns.evidence: hook_type comparison: 8% of all but 29% of top tier (lift 3.43), median 400,987 views; relatable_scenario lift 3.43, median 630,623; story_tease lift 3.43, median 513,347 — versus bold_claim at lift 0.38, median 42,366. Named examples: "Mask on Mask off" (540,836), "High Collagen" (261,137), "My mask" (630,623), "Real eyes.." (513,347).
winningPatterns.howToApply: Open on a state-vs-state device (mask on / mask off, 6am / 6:20am, patch side / bare side) or a lived moment ("My mask"), never on a benefit statement.

winningPatterns.pattern: Deliver the before/after as the payoff inside the carousel, not as the hook line
winningPatterns.evidence: before_after hooks are 29% of all and 29% of top tier — lift 0.98, median 71,901 views — while comparison (lift 3.43, median 400,987) and relatable_scenario (lift 3.43, median 630,623) over-index in the top tier. The one huge before/after hook was highly specific: "Tired eyes Before Dark circles using the Abib Collagen Eye Cream, swipe to see what my under eyes area looks like now!" (1,018,053 | 39.4x).
winningPatterns.howToApply: Hook with the scene; reveal the split-screen on slide 4 or 5. If you must label a before/after up front, name the product and add an explicit swipe instruction, as the 1,018,053-view hook did.

winningPatterns.pattern: The word 'collagen' is the niche's curiosity magnet — but only in short, non-listicle form
winningPatterns.evidence: Short collagen hooks broke out hard: "High Collagen" (261,137 | 4080.3x, 64 followers), "Collagen boosting" (113,465 | 88.1x), "Before and after Collagen" (71,901 | 62.7x), "40 days of collagen" (12,549 | 93.6x). Long claim versions collapsed: bold_claim lift 0.38, median 42,366 ("BEST BENEFITS OF COLLAGEN" 85,773; "5 Benefits of Collagen ☝️" 31,592).
winningPatterns.howToApply: Use two-word ingredient stamps ("High collagen", "Collagen boosting") as slide-1 text or as a repeated corner stamp, and explain the mechanism in one sentence on slide 3.

winningPatterns.pattern: Zero-follower accounts win this niche — the hook does all the distribution work
winningPatterns.evidence: 8 of 24 slideshows are small-account breakouts (<50k followers, >=50x follower views), including 64 followers -> 261,137 views (4080.3x, "High Collagen"), 1,460 -> 189,499 (129.8x), 4,850 -> 513,347 (105.8x, "Real eyes.."), 1,146 -> 71,901 (62.7x).
winningPatterns.howToApply: Ship formats that need no credibility scaffolding: no talking-head intro, no follower proof, no brand-lore slide. First panel = image + <=4 words.

winningPatterns.pattern: Editorial, no-CTA carousels are the norm — nothing in this corpus sells on-slide
winningPatterns.evidence: has CTA: no — 100% of all 24 slideshows and 100% of the 7 top-tier slideshows; CTA types list is empty. Median engagement 1.4%.
winningPatterns.howToApply: End on the payoff image or a one-line routine note instead of "link in bio"/"comment SHOP". Push conversion to caption and comments so the final slide stays a visual reward.

hookFormulas.whyItWorks: Directly modelled on "My mask" (630,623 views, 198.3x from 3,180 followers) — the highest-median hook type in the set (relatable_scenario, lift 3.43, median 630,623). Two words force the viewer into the image to find the story.
Modelled on "Mask on Mask off" (540,836 | 35.5x), a comparison hook — the type with lift 3.43 and a 400,987-view median. It promises a two-state reveal in four words.
Exactly the shape of "High Collagen" (261,137 views from 64 followers, 4080.3x) — the biggest outlier multiple in the dataset. An ingredient stamp, not a claim, so it dodges bold_claim's 0.38 lift.
Modelled on "Real eyes.." (513,347 | 105.8x), the only story_tease in the set (lift 3.43, median 513,347). The trailing ellipsis sells the swipe without explaining anything.
Lifted from "hey, mask!" (219,916 | 28.9x, direct_address). Talking to the product turns a product shot into a character and keeps the panel under three words.

hookFormulas.formula: [Symptom] before / [Symptom] after using [named product] — swipe to see [body area] now
hookFormulas.example: Puffy eyes before, flat under-eyes using the collagen hydrogel patches — swipe to see my morning face now
hookFormulas.whyItWorks: The only long hook that broke a million: "Tired eyes Before Dark circles using the Abib Collagen Eye Cream, swipe to see what my under eyes area looks like now!" (1,018,053 | 39.4x). Specificity plus an explicit swipe command is what carried it, since generic before/after hooks sit at lift 0.98.
Modelled on "40 days of collagen" (12,549 views but 93.6x follower outlier) — a time-bound frame that presells a dated proof grid instead of a claim.

slideStructure.recommendedSlideCount: 6 slides (brief-mandated); the data cannot confirm an optimal count — slide count is 'unknown' for 100% of the corpus
slideStructure.arc: Scene hook (<=4 words) -> the relatable problem moment -> the mechanism in one line (collagen/hydrogel doing the work) -> proof: split-screen or dated grid -> how it fits a real night/morning routine -> payoff close-up, no CTA
slideStructure.textDensity: Very low: 2-6 words per panel, one idea per slide, single large sans-serif line. Panel-word medians are n/a in this dataset, so this comes from the hook evidence — the top hooks average 1-4 words and the long claim hooks (bold_claim, lift 0.38, median 42,366) underperformed
slideStructure.visualStyle: Phone-shot, unretouched close-ups of the under-eye area with the patch clearly visible; two-state pairings (on/off, 6am/6:20am, bare side/patched side); soft bathroom or bedside lighting; ingredient stamp in the corner. Face-visible, background and foreground data are all 'unknown', so treat these as testable defaults, not proven
slideStructure.notes: Slide-level intelligence is missing for this niche: narrative_arc, text_density, content_format, emotional_tone, slide count, face visible, before/after, background, foreground and subject age are 'unknown' for 100% of all 24 items and 100% of the top tier, because all 24 sources are hook_corpus entries with no slide data. Structure guidance above is inferred from hook types, hook wording and view medians only. One confirmed structural fact: 0 of 24 slideshows used a CTA. Also note recency — 0 slideshows posted in the last 30 or 90 days, so treat these as evergreen formats and re-test rather than assume current feed behaviour.

contentAngles.title: Mask on / mask off
contentAngles.angle: A six-panel two-state loop: same face, same lighting, alternating patched and bare under-eyes across the morning, so the swipe itself becomes the transformation. Designer note: identical crop and camera distance on every slide so only the eye area changes, with the words 'on' and 'off' alternating in the same corner.
contentAngles.targetEmotion: Satisfying visual click — the pleasure of a clean two-state reveal

contentAngles.title: Real eyes at 6am
contentAngles.angle: Relatable-scenario diary of one badly-slept morning: creased, puffy, dark under-eyes timestamped 6:02am, patches applied 6:05am, coffee, dog, 6:25am de-puffed. Designer note: timestamp overlays in the top-left of each panel, zero retouching, phone flash allowed.
contentAngles.targetEmotion: Recognition and relief — 'that is literally my face'

contentAngles.title: Hydrogel vs silicone
contentAngles.angle: Head-to-head comparison of single-use collagen hydrogel patches versus reusable silicone patches: adhesion, slip, wear time, cost per wear, which one survives a 20-minute walk around the flat. Designer note: split every panel down the middle, left = hydrogel, right = silicone, one verdict word per slide.
contentAngles.targetEmotion: Decision confidence — settling a purchase debate in six swipes

contentAngles.title: High collagen, explained
contentAngles.angle: The mechanism angle told in stamps rather than sentences: what collagen and peptides actually do in the thin under-eye skin, why hydrogel drives it in, and why 15 minutes beats 3 minutes. Designer note: ingredient stamp repeated in the same corner of all six panels, one short line of copy per slide, macro shots of the patch texture.
contentAngles.targetEmotion: Smart-shopper curiosity — understanding the thing you already own

contentAngles.title: 40 nights of patches
contentAngles.angle: A time-bound consistency diary: night 1, 5, 12, 25, 33, 40 shot in the same mirror at the same time, with one honest note per date (what changed, what did not). Designer note: date badge burned into every photo, no filters, final panel is the two extremes side by side.
contentAngles.targetEmotion: Earned trust — proof that looks like a receipt, not an ad

carouselBriefs.concept: Six identically framed close-ups alternate between bare and patched under-eyes across one morning, so swiping physically toggles the transformation. Slides 3 and 5 add a single word each — 'flat', 'awake' — while the product stays anonymous until the last panel. The whole carousel teaches one thing: 15 minutes of wear visibly changes the eye area.
carouselBriefs.audience: Women 25-38 who apply makeup on tired eyes before work and hate how concealer creases

carouselBriefs.concept: A timestamped one-morning diary starting with unretouched 6:02am puffiness and ending at 6:25am after collagen hydrogel patches, coffee and cold water. Each slide is one moment with one short line, and the mechanism gets a single sentence on slide 4. It shows the routine as it actually happens, not as a tutorial.
carouselBriefs.audience: Women 30-45 who wake up with puffy, creased under-eyes after 5 hours of sleep

carouselBriefs.concept: A six-slide split-screen showdown between single-use collagen hydrogel patches and reusable silicone patches, judged on grip, wear time, comfort under makeup, cost per wear and travel. Each panel delivers one verdict word so the reader can stop at any slide and still have an answer. The final panel names which one to buy for which morning.
carouselBriefs.audience: Value-conscious skincare buyers 22-35 deciding between a subscription patch pack and one reusable set

avoid: Bold-claim and benefit-listicle hooks. bold_claim is 38% of all slideshows but only 14% of the top tier (lift 0.38) with a median of just 42,366 views — e.g. "BEST BENEFITS OF COLLAGEN" (85,773), "5 Benefits of Collagen ☝️" (31,592), "Marine collagen 🔥" (12,557).

Question hooks. 8% of all slideshows, 0% of the top tier (lift 0), median 187,471 — "WHY IS COLLAGEN IMPORTANT?" (189,499) and "why are eye patches so popular these days?" (185,443) both plateaued below the 261,137-view top-tier threshold.

Generic, product-free before/after labels. before_after hooks sit at lift 0.98 (median 71,901) and the worst performer of the whole set was "COLLAGEN BEFORE & AFTER" (47,442, 0.5x). If you label a before/after, name the product and add a swipe instruction like the 1,018,053-view hook did.

Chasing the dataset's #1 post. "It Girl" Watches Under $300 (1,197,741 | 2037x) is off-niche accessory bait, not eye-mask content — it inflates the max/p90 and is not replicable or on-brand for a skincare account.

On-slide CTAs and sales panels. 0 of 24 slideshows, including 0 of the 7 top-tier posts, used any CTA (CTA types list is empty); keep 'link in bio' and discount codes in the caption so slide 6 stays a visual payoff.

Off-niche collagen spillover topics. "Homemade Collagen Powder" (42,366), "COLLAGEN RICH SKIN JUICES" (141,411) and "Collagen Hair Repair before" (10,364) pull ingestible/hair audiences that do not convert to under-eye patches, and ingestible-collagen efficacy claims are a brand-safety risk.
